title: Compile paths for hybrid attention architectures (MHA / GQA / MoE): kernel selection & tuning
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Context: As part of onboarding new model families to the catalog we need canonical compile and kernel-selection strategies for three hybrid attention classes we regularly see in customer models: multi-head attention (MHA) variants, gated-query attention (GQA) hybrids, and sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE). Problem: default kernel heuristics choose suboptimal codepaths for some combinations of head count, kv-cache layout, and expert routing, causing 10–40% token throughput regression on H100/A100 and inconsistent latency at short sequences. Goals: 1) Define a deterministic compile-path map (graph of kernel candidates and fallback) per architecture family. 2) Implement compile-time flags and runtime selectors so onboarding can pin a model to a verified profile. 3) Publish performance profiles to the model catalog (latency, tokens/s, memory footprint, quantization compatibility). Success criteria: measurable throughput uplift or variance reduction vs current baseline and safe fallbacks for regressed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Formal compile-path mapping created for MHA, GQA, and MoE families and checked into runtime-config repo
Automated testbench runs that exercise primary and fallback kernels across target GPUs (A100/H100) with sequence lengths 32/128/1024
Published performance profile JSON for at least two representative models (one MHA variant, one MoE variant) in model-catalog with tags for quantization and memory envelope
No more than 5% P95 latency regression for pinned profiles vs baseline in canary environment; otherwise automatic fallback to reference kernels
Documentation and quickstart for model-onboarding engineers describing how to pin a profile and interpret profile metrics
tasks: Inventory kernels: flash-attn variants, Triton custom MHA, fused QKV, GQA-specific kernels, expert-routing kernels for MoE
Add microbench harnesses to perf-runner for head counts {8,16,32}, embed dims {512,1024,2048}, seq lens {32,128,1024}
Implement compile-time feature flags and annotate kernels with capabilities (kv-layout, causal-mask-optimized, fused-softmax)
Expose runtime heuristic toggles and allow explicit model-profile pinning via model metadata
Run full benchmark matrix on infra (A100/H100) and capture tokens/s, GPU memory, kernel occupancy
Create profile generator that converts benchmark CSV to model-catalog JSON + human-readable notes
Add unit and regression tests to prevent accidental compile-path changes without review

rollout_plan: 1) Publish profile for MHA 512d-head8 to model-catalog as 'mha-512-head8-v1' and pin for internal canary (10% traffic). 2) Monitor token throughput, P95 latency, and error rate for 48h. 3) If regressions >5% P95, auto-fallback to 'mha-reference'. 4) After validation, bump to 50% then 100% and mark as stable. MoE/GQA profiles follow same pattern; do MoE in isolated capacity pool due to memory envelope.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive fused kernels yield highest throughput at mid/long seq lengths but worsen short-seq latency; quantized kernels sometimes require slightly different memory layouts and may not support all fused ops. Plan to publish multiple named profiles per model (e.g., throughput-optimized, latency-optimized, quantized-compatible) and expose recommended default in onboarding checklist. If a model's architecture mixes GQA + MoE, use conservative profile that favors stability unless customer requests throughput profile.
